intitule: Spell Your Name and a Cameroonian City

enonce.texte:
Objective: Practice spelling using the English alphabet.

Instructions: Spell the following aloud:

  1. Your first name
  2. Your last name
  3. The city where you live (e.g., Yaoundé, Douala, Bamenda)
  4. A famous Cameroonian footballer (e.g., Eto'o, Nkoulou)

questions.texte: Spell the city where you live aloud.
Spell a famous Cameroonian footballer's name aloud.

enonce.texte:
Instructions: Practise the /θ/ (unvoiced) and /ð/ (voiced) sounds.

  • /θ/ (unvoiced): tongue between teeth, push air out.
  • /ð/ (voiced): tongue between teeth, vibrate vocal cords.

Read the following words aloud. Classify each word with the correct TH sound:

  • Words: think, this, that, three, mother, father, birthday, weather, thank, there

questions.reponse: this, that, mother, father, weather, there

enonce.texte:
Objective: Practise the /h/ sound in English. In English, the /h/ is always pronounced, unlike in French.

Instructions: Read the words below. Choose the correct pronunciation for each word.

  • house - /haʊs/ or /aʊs/
  • hello - /hɛˈloʊ/ or /ɛˈloʊ/
  • happy - /ˈhæpi/ or /ˈæpi/
  • holiday - /ˈhɑlədeɪ/ or /ˈɑlədeɪ/

Instructions: The English /r/ is different from the French /r/. The tongue does NOT touch the roof of the mouth. It is retroflex (tongue curled back).

Read the following words aloud. Pay attention to the /r/ sound.

  • red - /rɛd/
  • car - /kɑr/
  • very - /ˈvɛri/
  • around - /əˈraʊnd/
  • brother - /ˈbrʌðər/

questions.texte: Read the word 'red' aloud. How does your tongue move?
questions.reponse: The tongue curls back slightly, does not touch the roof of the mouth.

questions.texte: Read the word 'car' aloud. How does the /r/ sound at the end?
questions.reponse: The /r/ is pronounced softly, not rolled.

intitule: Minimal Pairs in Context - Complete the Sentence

enonce.texte:
Objective: Use minimal pairs to complete sentences correctly.

Instructions: Choose the correct word from the pair to complete each sentence.

  • Pair 1: sheep / ship - The ______ is sailing on the sea.
  • Pair 2: bed / bad - I feel ______ today.
  • Pair 3: see / she - Can you ______ the moon?
  • Pair 4: tree / three - There are ______ apples on the table.
  • Pair 5: sock / shock - I love to wear this ______.

enonce.texte:
Objective: Practise pronouncing your name and basic information correctly.

Instructions: Introduce yourself to the class using the following structure. Pay attention to pronunciation of each word.

“My name is ______. I am from ______. I am ______ years old.”

Example: “My name is Maria. I am from Yaoundé. I am 20 years old.”

questions.reponse: Example: My name is John. I am from Douala. I am 22 years old.

Instructions: Your teacher will say a word aloud. The first student to spell it correctly wins a point. Be careful with the pronunciation!

Words to spell (teacher's list):

  • school

  • brother
  • teacher

  • English

questions.texte: Spell the word your teacher says.
questions.reponse: Answers will vary depending on the word said by the teacher.

enonce.texte:
Objective: Practise difficult sounds in a fun way.

Instructions: Read the tongue twisters aloud as fast and as correctly as possible.

  • TH sound: “Three thirsty tigers think they are thirsty.”
  • H sound: “Harry has a happy holiday with his hat.”
  • R sound: “Red roses run along the road.”
  • Minimal pairs: “She sells sea shells by the sea shore.”

questions.reponse: Three thirsty tigers think they are thirsty.
Harry has a happy holiday with his hat.
Red roses run along the road.

questions.texte: Read the minimal pairs tongue twister.
questions.reponse: She sells sea shells by the sea shore.
